title: Model Channel Sentiment Mosaic & Rapid Fallback Prioritization
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Why: As competing LLM providers change availability, pricing, and latency, sales and SRE teams need a compact, signal-driven view that ties channel sentiment (availability, pricing churn, SLA noise) to prioritized fallback actions for customers. This ticket builds the product-facing artifact and operational pipeline that translates multi-source model-supply signals into a prioritized fallback catalog and handoff playbooks for Sales/SE and Ops.

What we'll deliver: (1) a taxonomy of channel sentiment signals (availability, price spikes, latency volatility, feature regressions, contract cadence), (2) an automated ETL that pulls signals from telemetry (usage telemetry + provider status pages + pricing feeds + partner Slack), (3) a lightweight dashboard with two views — a Mosaic (heatmap) of signal strength by region/channel/model and a Prioritization panel that maps customers and routes to recommended fallback actions, (4) an alerting rubric and runbook templates for Sales/SE/Customer Success, (5) a small synthetic workload experiment harness and postmortem template for validating fallback correctness.

Success metrics: detection-to-action time < 4 hours for P1 supply shocks; prioritized fallback accuracy >= 85% on a retrospective 6-week sample; Sales playbook adoption: 3 pilot customers run fallback flow in field tests; dashboard used daily by SRE/SE team.

Out-of-scope: deep model benchmarking of quality (we rely on existing Eval datasets), long-term procurement negotiations, and automated capacity provisioning (handled by Dedicated provisioning flow).
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy documented in Confluence with examples and ownership
ETL pipeline ingests at least 4 signal sources and populates normalized daily table
Mosaic dashboard shows region x model x channel view and supports filtering by tag
Prioritization panel outputs top-5 fallback actions per customer group and persists choices
Runbook templates and Slack escalation shortcuts added to ops playbook
Synthetic workload harness reproduces 3 outage scenarios and fallback succeeds without data loss
comments: 2025-01-28 - Evelyn Chen: Kickoff — scoped initial sources (provider status RSS, pricing CSV, usage telemetry, partner Slack channel). Agreed to MVP that surfaces historical volatility + current signal. Assigned Miguel as owner. Need ENG support for ETL (ENG-4210).

2025-02-03 - Miguel Torres: Initial taxonomy draft uploaded to Confluence. Traffic signals normalized to 'volatility' metric. Quick sync with Data Infra scheduled 2025-02-05 to confirm retention and table schema.
2025-02-07 - Priya Nair (Sales): Reviewed prioritization outputs; asked for customer-tagging by ARR bands and latency-SLA tiers. Added as stakeholder for playbook validation.
2025-02-11 - Data Infra (ENG-4210): Confirmed ability to pull pricing CSV and produce normalized feeds. Suggested moving volatility computation into materialized view for query performance.
2025-02-14 - Design: Provided initial wireframes for Mosaic heatmap and prioritized action card. UX comment: 'action cards must show rollback risk and expected latency delta.'

2025-02-18 - Miguel Torres: ETL PoC running nightly for two regions; dashboard prototype shows top-10 model-channel anomalies. Early false positives on short-lived provider flaps — plan to add smoothing and minimum-duration threshold.

2025-02-20 - Evelyn Chen: Reviewed prototype. Decision: include a manual override flag for Sales/SE to lock fallback choices per customer. Next: finalize smoothing logic, add ARR tiering, and schedule a pilot with two enterprise customers week of 2025-03-03.
risks: Signal noise generating high false-positive rate leading to alert fatigue
Data access limitations for some third-party pricing feeds
Insufficient engineering capacity to productionize ETL before pilot
Edge cases where fallback model degrades quality unacceptably for a given customer

Add ARR/latency tiers to prioritization logic (Owner: Evelyn)
